candidates.exact_span: The 4Q3 is 431.3 cubic feet per second (cfs) and the harmonic mean low flow used for human health calculations is 1108 cfs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 4Q3 and harmonic mean low-flow values feed dilution and human-health limit calculations; different interpretations of which flow statistic applies to a given parameter or period would change the computed applicable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: To convert 4Q3 expressed in cfs to 4Q3 expressed as MGD, the constant 1.548 cfs/MGD is used. The 4Q3 is 278.6 MGD and the harmonic mean low flow is 715.8 MGD.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conversion constant and resulting MGD flows are inputs to the critical dilution calculation; a different conversion factor or derived flow value would change dilution-based limit derivation.

candidates.exact_span: The NMWQS for total residual chlorine (TRC) are 11 ug/l for chronic and 19 ug/l for acute conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: These are the base water quality standards from which permit limits are derived; interpreting chronic versus acute applicability changes which numeric standard is selected.

candidates.exact_span: The NNWQS for TRC are 4000 ug/L for domestic water supply, and primary/secondary human contact; 19 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-acute; and, 11 ug/L for aquatic & wildlife habitat-chronic and livestock watering.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Multiple NNWQS values for different use classifications must be compared under the most-stringent-standard rule; interpretation of which use classifications apply to this discharge could change the selected limit.

candidates.exact_span: Since acute conditions do not allow dilution; the limit must be met at end-of-pipe but chronic standards do allow dilution, the permit shall use the most stringent WQS for the permit limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This rule governs whether dilution is permitted and which standard governs; different readings of acute versus chronic conditions or of the most-stringent-selection obligation would change the applicable enforceable limit.

candidates.exact_span: Qe = facility effluent or design flow; 6.67 MGD
candidates.computation_change_reason: Effluent flow is a direct input to the critical dilution formula; a different interpreted design or effluent flow would change the dilution factor and thus the derived limit.
Receiving-stream flow used as Qa in the critical dilution calculation; a different interpreted 4Q3 value would change the dilution factor and limit derivation.

candidates.exact_span: F = fraction of stream allowed for mixing; 1.0
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing-zone fraction is a multiplier in the critical dilution formula; interpreting whether 1.0 applies or a different fraction is authorized would change the computed limit.

candidates.exact_span: The in-stream TRC concentration after allowing for dilution is; 11 ug/l ÷ 0.0234 = 470 ug/l. Since this value is greater than the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute standard, the 19 ug/l is more stringent and will be more protective.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage records the comparison logic that selects the 19 ug/l limit over the dilution-adjusted chronic value; different interpretation of the comparison or arithmetic would change which numeric limit is deemed applicable.

candidates.exact_span: The draft permit maintains the 19 ug/l end-of-pipe acute limit since it is more stringent and will be more protective than the 11 ug/l dilution based chronic limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: States the selected enforceable numeric limit for TRC; whether this 19 ug/l end-of-pipe limit is operative for compliance comparison directly determines Purpose A outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: In addition to the 19 ug/l chemical specific limitation, the draft permit also maintains the narrative limit for total residual chlorine shall be “No Measurable.”
candidates.computation_change_reason: A narrative no-measurable limit coexists with the 19 ug/l numeric limit; interpretation of whether both are independently enforceable, and how they interact, would change which limit applies to a given measurement.

candidates.exact_span: TRC shall be limited as follows: “After dechlorination and prior to final disposal, the effluent shall contain NO MEASURABLE (TRC) at any time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The timing and process conditions ('after dechlorination and prior to final disposal') scope when the narrative limit applies; different interpretation of these conditions changes both the applicable limit (A) and how missing or conditional no-result periods are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: NO MEASURABLE will be defined as no detectable concentration of TRC as determined by any approved method established in 40 CFR Part 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The detection-limit-based definition determines what constitutes compliance or exceedance for the narrative limit and how non-detect or method-limited results should be interpreted when no ordinary numeric value is reported.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent limitation for TRC is the instantaneous maximum and cannot be averaged for reporting purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The limitation type (instantaneous maximum, no averaging) governs how reported measurements must be compared to the limit; a different reading of averaging or reporting rules would change exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: The maximum dechlorinated TRC shall be monitored daily by grab sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Establishes a daily grab-sampling monitoring frequency obligation for TRC; interpretation of whether this requirement was applicable during a given period changes monitoring-obligation findings.

candidates.exact_span: TRC shall be measured within fifteen (15) minutes of sampling.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Specifies a timing constraint on valid monitoring; different interpretation of whether samples outside this window satisfy the requirement affects whether monitoring was required and performed (B) and whether available results constitute adequate evidence (C).
